quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Mileage information and distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs tell you about motorist services. They show locations of rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

questions.question: What must you do at a yield sign?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let other traffic in your intended path go first. You may go without stopping if no other traffic is nearby. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same.
questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain your speed. Do not speed up. Allow the other vehicle to pass safely and return to your lane.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus stops on the road to load or unload children?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm extended. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn before moving. Make sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down hills on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Stay farther behind other vehicles than usual. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you don't have antilock brakes.

questions.question: How do defensive drivers think?

options.text: They believe other drivers will do the right thing.
They expect mistakes from others and are ready to react.
They expect nothing and give nothing to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They expect mistakes from others and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers watch for mistakes that other drivers might make. They are prepared to act quickly to avoid a crash.

questions.question: How should a driver handle the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers will obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always be prepared to yield to prevent a crash, even if you have the legal right-of-way.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the curb.
Turn them away from the curb.
Leave them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking downhill or on a street without a curb, turn them toward the curb.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagon-shaped sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: What must you do when you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs and cones warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive if you can walk in a straight line after drinking.
Your driving is not impaired if you are under the legal blood alcohol limit.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react to things you see or hear on the road. Even if you are below the legal limit, any amount of alcohol can make it harder to drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a flooded road ahead?

options.text: Check how deep the water is and cross slowly.
Drive straight through without stopping.
Turn around and take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and take a different route.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded areas. If you see a flooded road, turn around and find another way to your destination.

questions.question: Your car can hydroplane on wet roads at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Most tires can move water away at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide over the water like water skis.

questions.question: This sign means the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves right, then curves left.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mark where passing is not allowed. If a solid yellow line is next to you, you cannot pass. Sometimes both lines are solid, meaning no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, move all four wheels off the main road if you can.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is dashed, only drivers next to the dashed line can pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange, yellow, or bright jackets and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. This means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you are allowed to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle in your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines between traffic lanes mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic moves in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can completely cross the intersection.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can completely cross the intersection.
questions.explanation: Don't enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through before the light turns red, even if your light is green. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a collision.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to avoid collisions. Don't use it to tell slow drivers to speed up or move out of your way.
